check_links_in_text.description: Read every link out of a block of text, such as an email body, a support ticket or a form answer, and check them all at once. Use it to hold back a message whose links Google has flagged. None of the links are sent to Google.
check_links_in_text.display_str_template: Check the links in text with Google Safe Browsing.

results.summary: Google Safe Browsing has nothing on file against this link.
Google Safe Browsing flags this link for malware.

check_links_in_text.name: check_links_in_text

parameters.description: The text to read the links out of. Anything starting with http://, https:// or www. counts as a link; a bare 'example.com' is left alone, because so are 'README.md' and 'config.py'.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: Which kinds of threat should make a link come back as unsafe. Leave all four chosen unless you only want to act on some of them.
parameters.name: threat_types

all_safe.description: True when Google flagged none of the links it checked. This is the field to branch on.

checked_count.description: How many of them were actually checked. Lower than link_count when some were not web addresses, or when there were more than 100 of them.

dangerous_count.description: How many of the checked links Google flagged.

dangerous_urls.description: Just the flagged links, ready to drop into a message without looping over the results.

invalid_urls.description: Anything that was not a web address and so could not be checked either way. Usually empty.

link_count.description: How many separate links there were in total, after duplicates were removed.

results.description: One verdict per checked link, in the order given.

is_safe.description: True when Google holds nothing against this link. This is the field to branch on.

report_url.description: A link that opens Google's own site status page for this address, so a person can read the verdict first-hand.

summary.description: The verdict in one sentence, ready to put in a message.

threats.description: What Google has against the link, one entry per kind of threat. Empty when the link is safe.

label.description: The same threat written out, for example 'Phishing and deceptive sites'.

matched_url.description: What Google actually has on file, which may be broader than the link that was checked. 'example.com/' means the whole site is listed, not just this page.

threat_type.description: Google's own name for the threat: MALWARE, SOCIAL_ENGINEERING, UNWANTED_SOFTWARE or POTENTIALLY_HARMFUL_APPLICATION.

url.description: The link that was checked, exactly as it was given.

check_url.description: Ask Google whether a link is dangerous, and get back what it holds against it: malware, phishing, unwanted software or a harmful Android app. The link itself is never sent to Google.

description: Check whether Google considers a link dangerous before your workflow acts on it. Check one link, a whole list, or every link inside an email or a message, and get back whether Google flags it for malware, phishing, unwanted software or a harmful Android app. The links are never sent to Google: only a few bytes of each one's fingerprint leave the workflow, which is the same protection Chrome itself uses.
